title: Furthest Point From Origin
summary: Given a string of length n consisting of 'L', 'R', and '_', representing movements on a number line starting from 0, where 'L' or '_' means move left, and 'R' or '_' means move right, return the distance from the origin of the furthest point reachable after n moves.
statement: Given a string of length n consisting of 'L', 'R', and '_', representing movements on a number line starting from 0, where 'L' or '_' means move left, and 'R' or '_' means move right, return the distance from the origin of the furthest point reachable after n moves.
constraints: Start at position zero on a number line.
L moves one unit left, R moves one unit right, and each underscore may be replaced independently by L or R.
Return the greatest possible absolute distance from the origin after all moves.
hints: First compute the signed displacement forced by L and R.
Every underscore can be aimed in whichever direction increases the final magnitude.
Choose all wildcards in the direction of the fixed displacement, giving abs(R-L)+underscores.
No wildcard can add more than one to absolute distance, and this construction adds exactly one for each, so it is optimal.
